“User is not defined” is a ReferenceError. The top of your file is missing a few things, and there’s one typo.

Your pasted file starts at module.exports, so it has neither the require for the User model nor the two helper functions. Without them, POST fails with “User is not defined”, and GET with query parameters would fail the same way because parseJson and parseNum aren’t defined either.
2. Fix the typo. In the POST handler, change User.findone( to User.findOne(. The capital O matters, and without it you’d get “findone is not a function” right after fixing the first error.
3. Two small spec fixes (they won’t cause errors now, but the autograder checks the format):

In the two 400 responses for name and email, add data: {}, since every response needs both message and data. For example: res.status(400).json({ message: 'Name is required and must be a non-empty string', data: {} }).
In the POST catch, don’t send error.message to the client. The spec says never to leak database errors. Use:
This also prints the real error in your terminal, which helps while debugging.
Then save, restart npm start, and send the same POST again. You should get a 201 with the user. Send it a second time and you should get a 400 for the duplicate email.

email: { type: String, required: [true, "email is required"], unique: true },

That’s the template’s original version, and it still works, but only by accident. Here’s why, and the cleaner version to use.

router is one shared object. Your first app.use('/api', ...) already mounts every route registered on it, including users, so /api/users works. The second line mounts the same router again at /api/users, which creates a duplicate set of paths like /api/users/users. It’s harmless but messy. It also has no line for tasks, so routes/tasks.js isn’t being loaded at all.

Check that http://localhost:3000/api/users still works too.
